description: Directory of legitimate browser-game platforms and developer sites. Verified September 2026. Game counts are only shown where reliably attributable, and are marked as estimates.

sites.name: itch.io
sites.description: The indie game marketplace with a huge 'play in your browser' section — jams, experiments, demos and full games.
sites.details: Most browser games on itch.io are free or pay-what-you-want; playing requires no account. Thousands of game-jam entries from Ludum Dare and GMTK Jam are hosted here.
sites.gameCountNote: Not published as a browser-playable figure; total projects exceed one million (platform statistic).
sites.mobileNote: Some games support touch; catalog is desktop-first.

sites.name: CrazyGames
sites.description: A large, fast, ad-supported portal for free browser games — everything from io hits to 3D shooters.
sites.details: No account needed to play; the portal is desktop and mobile-web friendly and licenses/publishes many exclusives.
sites.gameCountNote: Approximate, per platform's own claims.

sites.name: Poki
sites.description: The mobile-web-first games platform — the official web home of Subway Surfers, Retro Bowl and hundreds of exclusives.
sites.details: Poki's 'online games on Poki' model focuses on instant play on any device. Its partnerships (e.g. with SYBO, announced/expanded November 2025) bring major mobile franchises to the browser.
sites.gameCountNote: Not published; a large, curated catalog of roughly a thousand-plus titles.

sites.name: Game Jolt
sites.description: An indie community platform with a large browser-playable section, game jams and creator support.
sites.details: Many indie games run directly on the site for free (account optional). Beware copycat domains like 'gamesjolt.net' — the official site is gamejolt.com.
sites.gameCountNote: Not published (browser-playable subset of a very large indie catalog).

sites.name: Y8
sites.description: One of the longest-running game portals, hosting tens of thousands of browser games old and new.
sites.details: Y8 has run since 2006 and retains an enormous archive of HTML5 and legacy titles. Free with ads; account optional.
sites.gameCountNote: Tens of thousands of titles (long-running archive); exact figure not published.

sites.name: Newgrounds
sites.description: The legendary independent flash/HTML5 portal that launched careers — games, movies and art since 1995.
sites.details: Everything from indie classics (Henry Stickmin, Alien Hominid) to modern web games. Free; account optional but core to the community.
sites.gameCountNote: Not published; tens of thousands of games and animations across 30 years.

sites.name: Kongregate
sites.description: The classic portal's 128,000+ legacy game library remains playable, though new uploads ended in July 2020.
sites.details: Kongregate stopped accepting new games and retired most social features in 2020, shifting focus to publishing; the existing library (much of it HTML5 or Ruffle-emulated Flash) is still available to play.
sites.gameCountNote: Per Kongregate's July 2020 announcement (uploads ended; existing library playable).

sites.name: Armor Games
sites.description: A curated portal of over a thousand browser games, home of Kingdom Rush, Sonny and GemCraft.
sites.details: Founded in 2004 and still active with HTML5 ports of classic series. Free with ads; account optional.
sites.gameCountNote: Per Wikipedia (HTML5 + legacy titles).

sites.name: Addicting Games
sites.description: A long-running portal with 5,000+ free games across every casual genre.
sites.details: Still actively updated with indie spotlights and demos. Free with ads; account optional.
sites.gameCountNote: Per platform's own claims.

sites.name: Coolmath Games
sites.description: The school-friendly portal for thinking games: puzzles, logic, strategy and classic skill games.
sites.details: Aimed at all ages with a 'brain-training' angle; widely whitelisted in schools. Free with ads; no account needed to play.
sites.gameCountNote: Not published; large curated catalog.

sites.name: FRVR
sites.description: The instant-games publisher behind hits like Krunker and MooMoo.io, playable straight from the browser.
sites.details: FRVR operates a slate of HTML5 games and acquired Krunker.io (2023) and MooMoo.io. Its site hosts its own catalog with no download required.
sites.gameCountNote: Not published; dozens of first-party instant games.

sites.name: Nitrome
sites.description: The beloved UK studio's own site — play 100+ of their pixel-art classics free in the browser.
sites.details: Nitrome has converted dozens of its Flash-era classics to HTML5 (in partnership with Poki) and continues to release new games.
sites.gameCountNote: Approximate count of Nitrome's own games.

sites.name: Flipline Studios
sites.description: The official home of the Papa's games — the entire time-management series, free in your browser.
sites.details: Flipline hosts remastered HTML5 versions of Papa's Pizzeria, Freezeria and the rest of the series on their own site, no account required.
sites.gameCountNote: The Papa's series plus other titles.

sites.name: Bart Bonte
sites.description: Award-winning independent puzzle designer — play the color series, Factory Balls and more, free.
sites.details: Bart Bonte's site links his browser games (blue, green, sugar, sugar, Factory Balls…) alongside his mobile and Steam releases.
sites.gameCountNote: Approximate count of browser-playable titles.

sites.name: neal.fun
sites.description: A collection of wildly creative interactive toys and games: Infinite Craft, The Password Game and more.
sites.details: Neal Agarwal's projects regularly go viral; each is a small, polished browser experience — free with no account.
sites.gameCountNote: Approximate count of interactive projects.

sites.name: Board Game Arena
sites.description: Play 1,000+ real board games online with friends — from Carcassonne to 7 Wonders, officially licensed.
sites.details: The world's largest board-game platform runs in the browser with real-time and turn-based play. Free account required to play; some premium games need a subscription.
sites.gameCountNote: Per platform's own claims.

sites.name: CardGames.io
sites.description: Clean, no-nonsense versions of Hearts, Spades, Solitaire and dozens of other classics.
sites.details: Simple, fast, ad-light and account-free — the anti-portal of card and board games.
sites.gameCountNote: Approximate count of titles.

sites.name: PBS Kids Games
sites.description: Free, safe educational games for children featuring PBS Kids characters — no account, no ads.
sites.details: A trustworthy option for younger players: hundreds of age-appropriate learning games that run in any browser.
sites.gameCountNote: Hundreds of titles; exact figure not published.

sites.name: Internet Archive: Internet Arcade
sites.description: Hundreds of classic coin-op arcade games from the 1970s–90s, emulated in your browser.
sites.details: Run by the nonprofit Internet Archive using in-browser MAME emulation. Availability of individual titles varies as rights-holders request removals — it's a digital library, not a store.
sites.gameCountNote: Hundreds of titles; the collection changes over time as items are added or removed at rights-holders' request.

sites.name: Internet Archive: MS-DOS Games
sites.description: Over 6,000 DOS-era games — Oregon Trail, Prince of Persia and more — bootable in the browser.
sites.details: The Internet Archive's Software Library runs thousands of MS-DOS titles via EM-DOSBOX. Same caveats as the Internet Arcade: it's a preservation library and some titles may be unavailable.
sites.gameCountNote: Per the collection's description.

sites.name: NYT Games
sites.description: Wordle, Connections, the Crossword, Strands and more from The New York Times' games desk.
sites.details: Daily puzzles are free (Wordle, Connections without archive); a NYT Games subscription unlocks the full archive and crosswords.
sites.gameCountNote: A daily puzzle slate rather than a fixed catalog.
